digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate, impact model versioning and calibration
propositions: The divergent_implementation axis fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings despite being the sole hard-override axis never formally calibrated, and 90% of 1,307 omitted-scope findings are graded none rather than catching the real divergence.

A G6 finding (epic c4ad-a93e-0613-408f) that would re-embed a corpus and wipe a database scored impact 0.0 and landed ADVISORY despite validity 0.8889 and blocking_enabled=true because the axis does not distinguish contradictions from cosmetic omissions.

Replacing the ordinal none|low|medium|high grades with a closed Literal set (contradicts_reality, omits_required_site, incomplete_enumeration, none) and applying hard floors only to the first two prevents a 113-finding over-fire while keeping the two load-bearing divergence kinds at 0.85.
The structural change requires excluding divergent_implementation from the generic _SEV01 contribution loop and adding DIVERGENCE_GRADE01 mapping to avoid silent 0.0 scoring of new symbolic grades.

ADR-0054 rejects purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review as calibration instruments, permitting only corpus replay and dogfooding under existing zero-marginal-cost data; this narrows ADR-0036's A/B clause while preserving version-segmentation and no-pooling rules.

A prod_impact floor (Fix 2) is rejected because it rescues findings across the novelty_priority_floor 0.4 threshold orthogonally to whether they are remediable, risking non-convergent loops, whereas Fix 1's semantic grades are inherently remediable by plan authors.
